newsitem.title: USA: Miami Gary firm denies involvement in fake letter.
newsitem.headline: Miami Gary firm denies involvement in fake letter.

text.p: Miami bond firm Howard Gary & Co issued a statement denying involvement in the alleged forgery of a letter purportedly written by bond firm owner Leo Guzman.
The letter accused one of Dade County's financial advisers, Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc, of violating a regulation against passing on certain municipal underwriting fees to issuers.
Rauscher Pierce denied the allegation and Guzman insisted he did not write the letter.
But county commissioners dismissed Guzman's firm in December from a $440 million water-sewer bond deal, saying that because of the letter "there is a shadow cast" on Guzman.
Guzman said Wednesday that phone records show a fax transmission of the letter was made from the Miami home of M.L. Parekh, whose son Kishor is senior vice president at Howard Gary & Co.
Guzman stopped short of directly accusing Gary's firm of involvement, but said the letter was clearly written by someone intimately familiar with the municipal bond industry.

Howard Gary, president of Howard Gary & Co, released a statement Thursday saying that the firm "considers the recently publicized events regarding a purportedly forged letter on Guzman & Co's letterhead as odious and offensive."

He also stated, "Although Howard Gary & Co was not a participant in this activity, it expresses its empathy to Guzman & Co and Raushcer Pierce Refsnes Inc for the problems and inconveniences such false accusations and allegations have caused. This industry should have no place for such contemptible acts."
Gary's firm was also dismissed from the Dade County bond deal because of concerns about Gary's role as a government witness in a federal probe of public finance corruption.
The deal was priced Thursday by PaineWebber Inc, with top yields of 5.734 percent.
